positions.name: Standing exchange
positions.top: Both athletes are upright and hand-fighting for grips, distance, and a safe entry. There is no top or bottom yet.
positions.bottom: Both athletes are upright. Choose a stable stance, protect your balance, and decide whether to engage, disengage, or pull guard.

positions.name: Collar tie & snapdown
positions.top: Use head and arm position to break posture, then follow the opponent toward a front headlock or a controlled takedown.
positions.bottom: Keep your posture, clear the tie, and avoid leaving your neck extended. A failed snapdown can become a guard pull or a re-shot.

positions.name: Body-lock clinch
positions.top: Connect around the torso while keeping your own head and hips safe; use steps and balance breaks to set up a takedown.
positions.bottom: Pummel for inside arm position, widen your base, and turn toward space before the lock closes. Follow your academy's takedown safety rules.

positions.name: Front headlock
positions.top: Control the head and near arm without hanging your weight on the neck; move toward a go-behind or a coached submission entry.
positions.bottom: Build posture with a frame, clear the head, and face your partner before they circle behind. Do not twist or yank the neck.

positions.name: Closed guard
positions.top: Break the leg lock with posture and safe hand placement, open the ankles, then stand or kneel into a planned guard pass.
positions.bottom: Keep your legs connected around the waist, manage posture with grips or frames, and create an angle before sweeping or attacking.

ref.credit: Photo by MartialArtsNomad.com via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0

positions.name: Open guard (general)
positions.top: Keep your posture and balance while clearing the feet and knees. Pass one layer at a time; don't dive past active hooks.
positions.bottom: Use your legs, shins, and frames to keep distance, recover inside position, and choose a named guard that fits the grips and distance.

positions.name: Spider guard
positions.top: Manage sleeve grips and clear the feet from your arms before stepping around the hooks. Keep posture as you pass.
positions.bottom: Use sleeve grips and feet against the arms to manage distance and off-balance. Bend one leg while extending the other; keep your hips active.

ref.credit: Photo by soh32's via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA / GFDL

positions.name: Lasso guard
positions.top: Free the lassoed arm safely, keep your elbows close, and avoid turning into the hook before you have cleared it.
positions.bottom: Thread a leg around the sleeve arm and keep your knee-to-elbow connection; use the lasso to slow the pass and create an angle.

positions.name: Butterfly guard
positions.top: Control the legs and upper body before driving around the hooks. Avoid leaning forward with your arms posted far away.
positions.bottom: Sit with inside position and active hooks. Break balance forward or to a side, then come up behind a sweep or arm drag.

ref.credit: U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Jeff Sisto via Wikimedia Commons · Public domain

positions.name: Seated open guard
positions.top: Close distance without giving up a collar tie or underhook; clear the legs before committing to a pass.
positions.bottom: Stay balanced on your hips, use frames and inside ties, and connect to butterfly, shin-to-shin, or a wrestle-up when distance allows.

positions.name: De La Riva guard
positions.top: Control the hook and keep your trapped leg free of the outside angle. Turn to face the guard player before passing.
positions.bottom: Use the outside hook and complementary grips to manage a standing passer; off-balance before choosing a sweep or back-taking route.

positions.name: Reverse De La Riva
positions.top: Recognise the reverse hook, keep your knee line safe, and face the guard player before trying to backstep or clear the hook.
positions.bottom: Use the reverse outside hook to follow a passer who turns away; connect it to seated guard, wrestle-ups, or a back exposure.

positions.name: Half guard
positions.top: Keep your head and shoulder position, free the trapped knee, and avoid letting the bottom player establish an underhook.
positions.bottom: Protect your inside elbow, turn onto your side, and build a frame or underhook before attempting to come up.

positions.name: Knee-shield half guard
positions.top: Control the knee shield before closing distance; choose a safe route around the frame or back out to reset.
positions.bottom: Use the shin as a frame, protect your head space, and recover guard or win an underhook when the passer changes pressure.

positions.name: Deep half guard
positions.top: Keep your hips back and balance wide; avoid letting the bottom player get underneath your centre of gravity.
positions.bottom: Stay connected under the hips with your head safe. Use coach-guided sweeps to come up or expose the back rather than lifting with your neck.

positions.name: X guard
positions.top: Manage the hooks and keep your weight centred over your feet. Step to clear the structure rather than hopping blindly.
positions.bottom: Control a leg with your hooks and grips, then off-balance in more than one direction to create a technical stand-up or sweep.

positions.name: Single-leg X / ashi garami
positions.top: Recognise the leg configuration and disengage safely. Follow the rules for your belt, age, and competition division.
positions.bottom: Use the configuration as a control and off-balancing position. Learn entries, exits, and legal options with your coach before studying submissions.

positions.name: K guard
positions.top: Keep your knee line clear and posture balanced; step back or disengage when the inside position is compromised.
positions.bottom: Use the knee-shield-like frame and inside angle to connect to a leg-control position or return to open guard. Advanced entries require direct coaching.

positions.name: Octopus guard
positions.top: Keep your posture and avoid letting the seated player wrap behind your torso; clear the connection before driving forward.
positions.bottom: From a seated connection, wrap around the torso only when the distance and arm position are right. Stay attached through a coached back-take or sweep reaction.

ref.credit: Tullius Demosthenis via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 4.0 (cropped / blurred screenshot)

positions.name: Headquarters passing hub
positions.top: Pin one leg while keeping a strong upper-body connection. Choose a knee cut, leg weave, smash, or reset based on the frames.
positions.bottom: Prevent the passer from pinning your knee line; recover inside position or connect to a named guard before they settle pressure.

positions.name: Toreando / bullfighter pass
positions.top: Control both legs or pant grips, step outside the hooks, and circle around without letting the knees follow your hips.
positions.bottom: Keep your feet and knees tracking the passer, frame at the shoulders, and recover an inside hook before they settle side control.

positions.name: Knee-cut pass
positions.top: Win head-and-arm position, cut your knee across the thigh line, and free the trapped foot only when your upper-body control is secure.
positions.bottom: Frame across the collarbone and hip; turn onto your side and keep your knee inside so the passer cannot flatten you.

positions.name: Leg-drag pass
positions.top: Move both knees across your centre line and pin the hips before walking around; stay ready for the bottom player to turn in.
positions.bottom: Keep your shoulders facing the passer, recover a knee shield or underhook, and turn toward them before the hip pin settles.

positions.name: Over-under pass
positions.top: Control one leg over and one leg under while keeping posture and head position; walk around the hips rather than lifting with your back.
positions.bottom: Frame at the shoulder and hip, turn toward the underhook side, and recover a knee line before your hips are pinned.

positions.name: Body-lock / chest-to-chest pass
positions.top: Connect around the hips after clearing inside frames; walk around the legs with your head safe and posture controlled.
positions.bottom: Keep elbows inside and knees between the bodies; frame the neck and hip to create space before the lock closes.

positions.name: Smash / half-guard pressure pass
positions.top: Pin the shoulders and hips before clearing the knee line; progress in small steps and avoid stacking the neck aggressively.
positions.bottom: Keep a frame between your head and the passer, recover an inside knee, and turn toward your underhook before flattening.

positions.name: Side control
positions.top: Keep chest-to-hip connection, control the head and near arm, and advance to mount, north-south, or a safe submission setup.
positions.bottom: Protect your neck and inside elbows. Build frames, turn onto your side, and recover a knee or underhook before bridging away.

ref.credit: U.S. Navy photo by MC1 Brian A. Goyak · Public domain

positions.name: North-south control
positions.top: Stay connected around the shoulders and keep your hips heavy as you move past the head; transition back to side control if they turn in.
positions.bottom: Frame at the hip and shoulder, make space, and turn toward your partner only when your head and inside arm are safe.

positions.name: Knee on belly
positions.top: Balance through your base rather than crushing with the knee; use the reaction to move to mount, side control, or a controlled attack.
positions.bottom: Create a frame at the hip and shoulder, turn onto your side, and recover half guard or make a safe escape route.

positions.name: Mount
positions.top: Keep your base wide and chest balanced. Climb higher only when you have control; follow defensive turns toward technical mount or the back.
positions.bottom: Protect your neck, keep elbows connected, and escape in stages. Trap a post for a bridge-and-roll or create space for elbow-knee recovery.

ref.credit: U.S. Army photo by 2nd Lt. Robert Hundemer; retouched on Commons · Public domain

positions.name: S-mount
positions.top: A high mount variation used to isolate an arm. Keep your weight stable and follow your coach's controlled armbar or back-taking mechanics.
positions.bottom: Protect your elbow and shoulder, keep your hands connected to defend, and turn only when there is a safe route to recover guard or face your partner.

positions.name: Technical mount
positions.top: Use the angled base to follow a turning opponent and connect to back control or return to a stable mount.
positions.bottom: Hand-fight and keep your elbows inside; face your partner and recover a guard before they settle the seatbelt or hooks.

positions.name: Back control
positions.top: Keep your chest connected, seatbelt or equivalent control secure, and hooks or body triangle positioned without squeezing the partner unsafely.
positions.bottom: Defend the choking hand first, hand-fight, then work your shoulders to the mat and turn toward the safe side to escape.

ref.credit: Photo by 92.61.64.212 via Wikimedia Commons · Public domain

positions.name: Turtle / referee's position
positions.top: Keep weight distributed and avoid reaching around the neck. Break the base carefully or follow a turn toward side control or back control.
positions.bottom: Protect your neck and elbows, build a safe base, and choose a sit-out, stand-up, guard recovery, or coached roll based on space.

positions.name: 50/50 & leg-entanglement hub
positions.top: Learn the entanglement and knee-line risks first; disengage or clear the knee line according to your coach and ruleset.
positions.bottom: Treat the position as a control and transition map, not an invitation to crank. Entries and exits should be drilled slowly under qualified supervision.

positions.name: Armbar finish (submission outcome)
positions.top: If you are attacking, maintain controlled alignment and stop immediately when your partner taps or signals distress.
positions.bottom: If you are defending, tap early when your elbow or shoulder is isolated. Do not test a lock under pressure.

positions.name: Triangle choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Learn the setup and finish with a coach; release immediately when a partner taps or is unable to respond.
positions.bottom: Recognise the position and tap early. Never use a neck crank to escape.

positions.name: Kimura control (submission outcome)
positions.top: Use it as a controlled shoulder-isolation threat and release as soon as your partner taps.
positions.bottom: Keep your shoulder safe and tap early; do not explosively twist against a locked grip.

positions.name: Rear-naked choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Apply only with coach-taught control. Release immediately on a tap or loss of response.
positions.bottom: Defend early with hand-fighting and tap early if the choke is set. Do not wait to pass out.

positions.name: Straight ankle lock (submission outcome)
positions.top: Check division rules and learn a controlled finish with your instructor. Release instantly on a tap.
positions.bottom: Tap early to ankle locks; do not rotate or wrench to escape a locked foot and knee line.

positions.name: Guillotine choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Use a controlled front-headlock connection and release immediately on a tap; do not squeeze to prove a point.
positions.bottom: Protect your neck and posture early; tap promptly if the choke is set. Do not bridge or twist into pressure.

ref.credit: U.S. Army Field Manual 3-25.150 via Wikimedia Commons · Public domain

positions.name: Arm-triangle choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Keep shoulder pressure and head position controlled; release as soon as your partner taps or signals distress.
positions.bottom: Turn toward the pressure only with coached mechanics, protect your neck, and tap early if the choke is set.

ref.credit: Photo by Eric Langley via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0

positions.name: Ezekiel choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Use a coach-taught setup and apply gradually; stop on a tap and avoid cranking the neck or face.
positions.bottom: Recognise the forearm and sleeve threat early, hand-fight, and tap before pressure becomes painful.

positions.name: Cross-collar choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Set grips patiently and finish with coached control; release immediately when your partner taps.
positions.bottom: Address the first grip before the second is established; tap early rather than enduring neck pressure.

ref.credit: U.S. Army photo by Sgt. William A. Tanner via Wikimedia Commons · Public domain

positions.name: Bow-and-arrow choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Keep back control stable and make the collar grip progressively; release the instant your partner taps.
positions.bottom: Hand-fight the collar grip first, turn toward a safe shoulder, and tap early if the choke is closing.

positions.name: Baseball-bat choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Use a deliberate grip sequence and controlled rotation; stop at the tap and avoid wrenching the neck.
positions.bottom: Recognise the two-handed collar grip early, clear a hand, and tap as soon as the choke is applied.

positions.name: Omoplata (submission outcome)
positions.top: Control posture and the shoulder line before sitting up; release when your partner taps and do not torque a trapped arm.
positions.bottom: Keep your elbow bent and posture safe; roll only with a coach-taught escape and tap early if the shoulder is isolated.

ref.credit: Photo by Rettotako via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 3.0

positions.name: D’Arce choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Keep the head-and-arm connection while maintaining safe neck alignment; release immediately on a tap.
positions.bottom: Use early frames to make space and protect your neck; tap promptly if the choke is set.

positions.name: Anaconda choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Maintain a controlled front-headlock connection and finish gradually under instructor supervision.
positions.bottom: Defend before the arm is threaded deeply and tap early if the choke is closing; avoid forceful neck rolls.

positions.name: Loop choke (submission outcome)
positions.top: Use the collar grip with controlled timing and release immediately when your partner taps.
positions.bottom: Clear the collar grip early, keep your posture safe, and tap promptly if the choke is applied.
